### 2026-10-09 – Today I worked on downloading and setting up my 'workspace', downloading the necessary files and applications as indicated by Half Life and the Starbie Github docs.

**2h**

Today I worked on downloading and setting up my 'workspace', downloading the necessary files and applications as indicated by Half Life and the Starbie Github docs.
This involved setting up my venv `hack_club_venv`, implementing Hackatime for VScodium, creating a  new Github repo, adding the .zip care package to my repo, downloading  Lookout for Lapse, and downloading KiCad. I recorded my notes and findings into my `readme.md` in the `week1-starbie/` folder of my repo.

### 2026-10-11 – # New KiCad Project + hackatime troubleshooting

**5h**

# New KiCad Project + hackatime troubleshooting
## KiCad Schematic
Followed the documentation provided by Half Life for learning to create schematics on KiCad for the Starbie.
This part was pretty simple!!

![kicad_diagrams](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9qUBiwu7vGTPrZ3ZZEyMoUbw1zu2kdW3/e497b8f6f31030790d8ed65f9e2f048e4b0cd0a614f6421952a6c719ca7513fa.png)

However, I would request a small revision in the documentation where it instructs to add the DHT11 sensor: should also mention to add a resistor ('A' key, search: "R") and edit the voltage by hovering over the symbol and pressing the 'V' key, inputing the value as 10k.

## Troubleshooting kicad-wakatime
Downloaded kicad-wakatime.app from Hack Club's repository for MacOS, an app intended to help you log heartbeats on KiCad, since the default Hackatime only .
Unfortunately, I faced troublesome bugs when using this application that made me unable to log my time spend on KiCad:
- kicad-wakatime.app continues to ask for permissions to Screen & Audio Recording on the mac, despite it being granted in my Systems Settings;
- kicad-wakatime.app returns an error that there are multiple .kicadsch files present while there is only one present because it also counts the files in the .history/ folder, which updates with the project file every time the project is saved.

![permission](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9qUBiwu7vGTPrZ3ZZEyMoUbw1zu2kdW3/063425c5405cd18643f50f1b16617fa57931d819dd5bdf6e6ee7e728d4768207.png)

I was able to solve the first problem by using the Terminal to "perform an ad-hoc code signature" that bypasses the restrictions that MacOS tries to place on the app (refer to readme.md in my week1-starbie/ folder for code specifics). I don't exactly understand how this works and had to resort to prompting an LLM for debugging help. I don't think that the terminal commands I used have any detrimental consequence to my computer's security, although I should continue to perform caution in the future.
For the second problem, I had a lot of trouble but after finding out that the extra files were from .history/, was able to temporarily fix the error by deleting the .history/ folder before every instance of running the application (and restarting the application after every KiCad save). I didn't take screenshots of the second problem, so you can just imagine error messages in the Terminal and kicad-wakatime.app as well as my random bash commands.

This was ultimately the most frustrating part of the learning process, because this was an unwarranted and unexpected hinderance to my coding process and definitely ate up a lot of my development time. Additionally, it was frustrating because it meant that I was unable to log my time accurately onto Hackatime, seeing as my time spent on KiCad was not always recorded (and a lot of my time was spent off of KiCad, troubleshooting). Another thing I noticed was that Hackatime split my work into two projects, one called "biebie" (the folder holding my KiCad files) and another from its enclosing folder called "halflife-hackclub" (the local branch to my github repo). This was strange because the latter's logged time was primarily spent working on the same files as the former. There is currently no way to merge the two projects. I was interested in the Terra challenge, but it seems I may need to abandon it since it relies on hackatime hours...

## KiCad PCB Editor
I really enjoyed this part where I learned to use the KiCad PCB Editor to draw the boundaries of the PCB. I tried a few different techniques,

![differentdesigns2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9qUBiwu7vGTPrZ3ZZEyMoUbw1zu2kdW3/da66ff683d91dafe94cc8bb8e9f1088b667221ce431317c14d3abcb49ab81c10.png)
first building a few blocky, pixel stars out of rectangles to retrace the outline and settling on creating a star using the outline tool and using shape modification to fillet the edges into a rounded star. Youtube tutorials were very helpful in realizing the Layers feature when creating the boundaries.
![layers](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9qUBiwu7vGTPrZ3ZZEyMoUbw1zu2kdW3/0f5056b0e362a35c2ab60ed940409dde319fa745cfb66b0bbebdd30ef695d49b.png)
I also learned about DRC which evaluates the errors in your PCB boundary design, which I think was extremely helpful -- especially due to the markers.

![DRCmarkers](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9qUBiwu7vGTPrZ3ZZEyMoUbw1zu2kdW3/2a992d3a3ac03c3dea58d6254795ed73c3f8c5229b0976c91acb9a0bc4bbea38.png)

The 3D viewer was also great for visualizing the board.

![finalPCBboard](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9qUBiwu7vGTPrZ3ZZEyMoUbw1zu2kdW3/7577d4506fd230e9a428be14751f76b3b03a8fd4f9951d6ea58dcea4abf11c0f.png)

The editor's color palette is also very aesthetically pleasing in a sorta cyber punk kinda way.

I think this is all that I've gone through this week, although there might be some other details, which I will keep in the week1-starbie/readme.md in my Github repo. Thanks for reading!! :D
